artworks.title: Annunciation to the Shepherds
artworks.artist: Probably Netherlandish 17th Century
artworks.description: This is a drawing of several animals and celestial figures in a pastoral setting. The drawing shows a group of animals, including a goat and a sheep, with an angelic figure on a cloud above emitting rays of light. To the right, a person in flowing garments is gesturing upwards, while another human face is seen behind them. The scene is detailed, with linework creating textures on the animals' fur and the figures' clothing. The composition indicates a dynamic interaction between the earthly and the celestial.

artworks.title: Henry Fuseli
artworks.artist: Attributed to Inigo Barlow
artworks.description: The image is an engraving of Henry Fuseli, shown in profile facing right with his arms crossed in front of his chest. His facial features are distinct with a prominent nose and strong jawline, and his hair appears wavy and pulled back. He is dressed in a high-collared shirt with a cravat and a jacket. Adjacent to him are a painter's palette and brushes, along with leaves. The background is a textured oval frame against a plain background, and below the image, "Henry Fuseli" is inscribed along with the engraver and source details.

artworks.title: A Choral Band
artworks.artist: Lydia Bates after John Hamilton Mortimer
artworks.description: The image shows a detailed drawing of several people seated in a balcony or theater box. The individuals are closely positioned next to each other, facing forward. Many are reading from books or documents. The drawing features exaggerated facial features, exaggerated noses, distinctive expressions, and various hairstyles ranging from curly to straight, some tied back. The clothing appears formal with visible collars and elaborate shoulder decorations. One figure on the left in the lower section wears a distinctive hat or headpiece. The individuals do not wear visible jewelry but hold papers. The background hints at a crowded setting, possibly a theater or courtroom, with additional figures in the upper rows and engravings on the upper walls.

artworks.title: Two Fleeing Figures
artworks.artist: Lydia Bates after John Hamilton Mortimer
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two figures in a landscape with a temple. The image contains two central figures facing a classical temple structure surrounded by trees and foliage. To the right, there is a grand structure with a dome. The foreground is detailed with rocks and vegetation. The style of the drawing, characterized by delicate lines and shading, gives it an almost ethereal quality, capturing both the movement of the figures and the peaceful atmosphere of the landscape.

artworks.title: A Falling Giant
artworks.artist: William Bond after William Hilton I after Thomas Banks
artworks.description: The sculpture in the image depicts a human figure titled "A Falling Giant." The figure appears to be falling or reclining backward over rocky terrain. The sculpture is made of marble and features intricate details, showing muscular definition and a realistic human form. The figure is in a dynamic pose, with one arm extended and legs bent at the knees, conveying movement and struggle against gravity. The giant is portrayed as larger than life, suggesting significant scale and presence in the surrounding environment.

artworks.title: Thy Kingdom Come (Monument to Sir Thomas Barting)
artworks.artist: William Bond after Henry Corbould after John Flaxman
artworks.description: The sculpture depicts a group of figures. A central female figure is semi-reclining with her head gently tilted upwards. Surrounding her are several other figures, including cherubic children who appear to interact with the central figure, as well as other adult figures, some with wings. The figures are intricately arranged and entwined. The sculpture has a monochrome appearance, commonly associated with marble material, highlighting intricate details and contours. The artwork appears as a relief, with three-dimensional elements emerging from a flat background, allowing light to accentuate depth and form against the surface.

artworks.title: John Augustus Tulk
artworks.artist: Anthony Cardon after Joseph Slater
artworks.description: The image shows an illustration of a man seated from the waist up. The man is in profile, facing slightly to the right and is comfortably seated in a chair. He has a high forehead, prominent features, and short hair. He wears a high-collared shirt, waistcoat, and double-breasted coat typical of early 19th-century style. He holds a paper in his hand. The background includes a draped curtain and what appears to be a classical landscape with columnar structures and trees.

artworks.title: Leonard Euler
artworks.artist: John Chapman
artworks.description: This is an engraved portrait of a man showing his upper body. He is positioned in profile, facing left. The man's facial features include a prominent nose and defined cheekbones, with deep-set eyes and a thoughtful expression. His hair appears to be long and wavy, peeking out beneath a soft cap or turban that covers his head. He is dressed in a high-collared garment with a fur lining, and beneath, a light-colored scarf is elegantly draped around his neck. The background shows an intricate textured oval frame surrounding the man, set against a plain surface. Below the main oval portrait, there is a smaller rectangular scene depicting two individuals sitting at a table in a setting that suggests conversation or writing, with the name "Leonard Euler" inscribed beneath it, along with publication details.

artworks.title: Monument to William Pitt
artworks.artist: George Cooke after James George Bubb
artworks.description: The sculpture depicts a group of four figures in classical style. In the center, a commanding figure stands on top of the base, flanked by two standing figures. At the base, there is a seated figure leaning against a horse-like creature with a serpentine lower body. The scene is rendered in monochrome with fine lines, resembling a black and white illustration.

artworks.title: John Flaxman
artworks.artist: Attributed to William Camden Edwards possibly after John Jackson
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man captured from the mid-chest upwards. He is positioned facing slightly to his left but looking directly at the viewer. The man's facial features are characterized by defined cheekbones and a composed expression. His hair is dark and sparse, receding slightly, with some curls visible near his ears. He is dressed in a formal manner, wearing a dark coat with a broad lapel over a high-collared white shirt and a dark cravat tied at the neck. There is no visible jewelry or objects seen in the portrait. The background of the portrait is plain and dark. The entire image is set within a cream-colored border.

artworks.title: Robert Thornton, M.D.
artworks.artist: Samuel Freeman after William John Newton
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man, depicted from the chest up. He is slightly turned to his left but looks straight ahead with a serious expression. The man has neat, light-colored short hair styled back. He is wearing formal attire, including a double-breasted coat over a collared shirt with a white cravat. There are no visible accessories or objects. The background features an oval frame against a plain surface and includes an engraving notation at the bottom with details about the work, including the name "Robert Thornton, M.D." and publishing information from August 1, 1809.

artworks.title: Robert Undy
artworks.artist: William Nelson Gardiner after Richard Cosway
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait of a man shown from the chest up, positioned in an oval frame at the center of the page. He is facing slightly to the left with his head turned to the side in a profile view. His facial features include a strong nose and a focused expression. His hair is styled in a traditional 18th-century manner, appearing grey and neatly combed back. He is dressed in formal attire with a high-collared shirt, detailed vest or cravat, and a dark coat. Below the portrait is text identifying him as "Robt Udny, F.R.S." with additional decorative elements. Beneath this is a decorative coat of arms with two nude figures playing instruments on either side of a shield. The entire composition is framed with a rectangular border on aged paper.

artworks.title: John Forbes Mitchell
artworks.artist: M. Gauci after John James Masquerier
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man from the chest upwards. He has short, neatly combed hair with a light wave. His facial features include distinct brows, a pointed nose, and a subtle mustache. He is wearing a dark coat over a high-collared white shirt with a loosely tied cravat. There are no visible accessories or objects in his hands. The background is a plain, graduated shadow that enhances focus on the subject. The name "John Forbes Mitchell Esq." is written at the bottom of the image, along with a mention of "Thainston, Aberdeenshire."

artworks.title: Sir Thomas Lawrence
artworks.artist: William Giller after Sir Thomas Lawrence
artworks.description: The image is a portrait of a man facing slightly to his right while maintaining eye contact with the viewer. He has a round face with a high forehead, large expressive eyes, full lips, and dark, wavy hair. The man is wearing a dark jacket over a white shirt with an upturned collar, typical of 19th-century fashion. The background is plain and dark, emphasizing the man's features and formal appearance.

artworks.title: William Gunn
artworks.artist: Harriet Gunn after E.J. Turner
artworks.description: The image shows the upper half of a man's body in profile view, facing left. He is seated in a side-facing position with his arms not visible in the draped clothing. The man has a prominent nose and a balanced jawline, with short, neatly combed hair that recedes at the temples. He wears a high-collared coat with a textured pattern. The background is plain, consisting of fine lines and shading that highlight the figure's profile. Below the man, the engraving includes text identifying him as "Revd. Wm. Gunn Translator of Nennius &c. Delt. Octr. 1821."

artworks.title: William Gunn
artworks.artist: Harriet Gunn after E.J. Turner
artworks.description: The image is an illustration showing the upper half of a man's body in profile, facing left. His posture is upright with his shoulders and head slightly tilted. The man has prominent facial features, including a prominent nose and high forehead. He has short, curly, light hair, slightly receding at the temples. He is wearing a high-collared coat typical of the early 19th century, with detailed line work for texture. The background is plain. Signatures and text are present at the bottom right corner of the drawing.

artworks.title: Monument to Earl Howe
artworks.artist: Charles Heath after Henry Corbould after John Flaxman
artworks.description: The sculpture depicts a scene with four figures. The central figure is Earl Howe, standing confidently with one arm on his hip and the other holding a cape. He is dressed in a naval uniform. Seated beside him is a female figure in classical attire, possibly representing Britannia, holding a trident. On either side of these figures are two other female figures in flowing gowns. One is reaching upwards, and the other is seated and gazing outward. Maritime elements like a ship's prow and a lion are included, symbolizing naval power. The sculpture is illustrated in monochrome, possibly crafted from a stone-like material. The depiction is detailed with intricate folds in clothing and defined facial features, giving the sculpture a classical and regal aura.

artworks.title: Medicina - Theologia - Lex
artworks.artist: James Heath after John Flaxman
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two robed figures shaking hands. The scene is enclosed within a circular frame and features two draped figures standing atop a small platform. One figure is holding a long staff, while the other carries a book labeled "Lex". Above them, the title 'Theologia' is positioned at the apex of a triangle with a small winged creature depicted inside. The drawing's composition and classic attire evoke classical or neoclassical style and themes.

artworks.title: Medicina - Theologia - Lex
artworks.artist: James Heath after John Flaxman
artworks.description: The image shows two women in full body view, standing and facing each other while shaking hands. Both are in profile with their gazes directed at each other. The woman on the left has her hair styled in an intricate updo adorned with a band, and the woman on the right wears her hair up with a headband. They are both draped in long, flowing garments. The left woman stands beside an object resembling a long walking staff, while the woman on the right holds a thick book in her left hand. The background features a triangular shape at the top center, surrounded by radiating lines, with the words "THEOLOGIA," "MEDICINA," and "LEX" inscribed around the circular border of the image. The overall setting has a symmetrical, medallion-like appearance, with a bird depicted above the center of the triangle.

artworks.title: Abraham Rees
artworks.artist: William Holl I after John Opie
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man in 18th-century attire. He has white hair styled in curls with a composed expression. He is holding a document and sitting next to a table with writing implements. The background features patterned drapery.

artworks.title: Priestley
artworks.artist: William Holl I after Gilbert Stuart
artworks.description: The image depicts a man sitting from the waist up. He is facing forward with a calm expression. The man has prominent cheekbones, a Roman nose, and mid-length curly hair. He is wearing a high-collared shirt with a cravat and a dark coat. The background is a uniform dark color. Text at the bottom reveals that the portrait is a reproduction of a work by Gilbert Stuart.

artworks.title: Monument to John Hudleston
artworks.artist: Richard James Lane after John Flaxman
artworks.description: The sculpture features two human figures: one standing, the other seated. The standing figure is male and dressed in a classical robe, with his head bent forward and resting on his hand. The seated figure is female, leaning against the male figure, with her head turned towards him. The sculpture is surrounded by architectural elements and inscriptions, indicating it may be a memorial. The color of the sculpture is a pale, neutral tone, possibly marble. It is placed on a plinth with an architectural backdrop including an urn shape, and inscribed with the words "Thy will be done."

artworks.title: William Gunn
artworks.artist: Richard James Lane after John Flaxman
artworks.description: The image is a sketch of a man's profile with a prominent nose and chin, short wavy hair, a high-collared shirt, and a jacket with a broad collar. The drawing is set against a plain background, with no jewelry or objects.

artworks.title: William Gunn
artworks.artist: Richard James Lane after John Flaxman
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man from the chest upwards in a side profile. He has a neutral expression, detailed facial features, and short, thinning hair. The man is wearing a coat or jacket with a high collar and a garment beneath. The background is plain. The signature "Wm Gunn" is visible at the bottom, with some small text in fine print.
